column2: 1. What is your role in the club, and how many years have you been involved?
2. Which tools do your teams use to design, analyze, and store their bridges?
column3: AutoCAD and Inventor for design, SAP model and hand calculations for analysis, all information stored on team members' personal laptops and MS Teams

column2: 3. What were the largest challenges you faced when you first joined the club?
column3: Figuring out where to start, no large archive/database for comparing past designs, strategies, the build/design process, and competition results

column2: 1. What information regarding the club administration is most important to consolidate?
column3: Past bridge data: overall design, calculations/analysis performed, competition results, successes/failures, etc.

column2: 2. When you first became an executive or coach, what were your largest difficulties?
column3: Previously Finance executive, few difficulties there as the club's finances are straightforward; new co-chair position brought many difficulties: planning how to familiarize new members with how Troitsky works, identifying the most feasible bridge types (to keep students from being discouraged if their bridges do not perform well), getting information to members other than through in-person meetings

column2: 3. How would you like to see the software sub team integrated into the club administration?
column3: Dedicated team working closely with the co-chairs, executive team and coaches, similar to existing teams; designated lead who communicates regularly with the co-chairs, gives development updates, and works with other areas of the club to find improvements; long term, expand to support both technical and administrative sides of the competition; technical: interactive design tools where students input a bridge configuration, select design constraints, and get help with structural calculations, member forces and other engineering considerations (especially for students new to structural design); administrative: centralized team-management platform (milestone submission, deadline tracking, coach and executive feedback, progress monitoring) to streamline communication and reduce the number of separate platforms; since the executive team changes yearly, clear documentation, responsibilities and transition procedures needed so the Toolbox can keep being maintained; wants the software sub-team to be a permanent part of the club structure and the Toolbox a long-term resource

column2: 1. What tool have you found is the most accurate and useful in predicting your bridge's performance?
column3: Team's performance estimates not very accurate due to little material data for the composite material; SAP used to identify large weaknesses, tests run in SAP along with hand calculations to estimate the anticipated max load

column2: 2. How close to a model estimate do you expect your bridge's performance to be, including uncertainties?
column3: Expects performance reasonably close to the model estimate, accounting for uncertainty in material properties, joint strength and construction quality; suggested the Toolbox give an estimated performance range rather than a single value, so teams can compare designs, identify weaknesses and understand potential failure points

column2: 3. What are the most common reasons for bridge failures in your experience?
column3: Most commonly torsion; first year, disqualified on reaching max deflection so the failure was never seen; other years, bridge loaded asymmetrically (placement correct, manufacturing issue) so only one truss was loaded, causing it to twist and break

column2: 4. Does the club have models and recorded failure loads of past bridges that could be used to test the Toolbox?
column3: Some data available from the most recent couple of years; everything before about 3 years ago was never recorded by previous co-chairs/execs and is lost

column2: 1. Is there anything about the club's information or tools that we did not ask about?
2. Are there any items that you feel are important to include in the Toolbox that we have not discussed?
column3: Long term: interactive structural calculation tools (input bridge configuration and design constraints to estimate member forces, deflections and potential failure points); team management features (milestone submissions, deadlines, coach feedback, progress tracking); searchable database of previous designs, material testing results and construction techniques; aware not all of this is feasible this year, hopes the software side of Troitsky develops over the next couple of years
